$comment: Declared SSOT for pg_cron jobs on the remote project.
These are NOT created by migrations on purpose: cron.job is data, not schema,
and a migration would make every local stack and preview branch run production
This manifest plus audit-cron-schedule.mjs gives SSOT without that side effect.
dailyBudget exists because on 2026-09-06 voyage-auto-activate-cron ran every
minute, 1440 of 1873 daily executions, and starved the t4g.nano of CPU credits
until pg_cron could no longer start any job. Nothing in the repo stated a
cadence, so nothing could see it. The budget makes that visible in CI.
Raised 600 -> 900 on 2026-09-23 when finalize-expired-voyages was added
(+288/day, bringing the declared total to 841). Still under half of the
1873/day that caused the incident, and unlike that job this one's body is
near-zero cost when nothing is expired (a handful of small-table lookups
against 4-row clan_voyage and a double-digit-row clan_voyage_contributions -
If a future addition needs to push this further, re-check that reasoning
still holds rather than just bumping the number again.

jobs.name: voyage-auto-activate-cron
jobs.$why: Event-gated. drivers.sync_voyage_activation_job() switches this on only while a voyage is PENDING and off again once none are, so active=false is the normal resting state and its cadence comes from substrate.config rather than from here. The audit therefore does not assert schedule or active for it, and counts 0 toward dailyBudget because its steady-state cost is zero. The trigger on drivers.clan_voyage is the real control; this entry exists so the job cannot go missing unnoticed.

jobs.name: finalize-expired-voyages
jobs.$why: Added 2026-09-23. Was previously called from drivers.on_battle_recorded() on every battle-insert row that fell outside an active voyage window (~6,500 calls/day) instead of on its own schedule - a wall-clock deadline (has any voyage's end_at passed?) was being detected as a side effect of an unrelated domain event. Moved here, on the same 5-minute cadence as headhunter-epoch-guard, because the voyage banner's countdown UI refreshes once on expiry and does not retry (see Frontend-PWA/src/shared/composables/useCountdown.ts) - finalization latency is user-visible and needed a bounded replacement, not just removal. See 20260923225809_decouple_voyage_finalization_from_battle_trigger.sql.
